title: Northwind Compute Q3 revenue jumps 48% to $312 million
author: Hannah Price
text:
Northwind Compute reported third-quarter revenue of $312 million, up 48% from a year earlier, as demand for rented GPU capacity held up through the summer.

The GPU cloud provider said gross margin narrowed to 41% from 44% in the second quarter, reflecting lower hourly rates and the cost of bringing two new data centres online. Net loss widened to $27 million.

Northwind said contracted backlog rose to $1.9 billion, and that customers committing to multi-year reservations accounted for about 70% of revenue in the period.

"We cut prices because our costs came down, and volume has more than made up for it," said Marcus Hale, Northwind's co-founder. "Utilisation in October is the highest we have ever recorded."

The company guided fourth-quarter revenue of $330 million to $345 million, slightly above analyst expectations. Shares rose 8% in after-hours trading.

Analysts said the results eased concerns that this month's 22% cut in list prices would erode growth, although several cautioned that the price war among specialist GPU clouds is far from over.
